title: An irreversible port-Hamiltonian system conserves energy and creates entropy
rationale: The second law is the point of the irreversible extension (Ramirez, Maschke & Sbarbaro 2013), and sigma >= 0 alone is far too weak a test: a model that puts the heat flow in R instead of in a modulated skew J conserves ENTROPY and destroys ENERGY -- the exact inverse of thermodynamics -- while still reporting a plausible non-negative sigma, because sigma was computed from a formula rather than from the dynamics. This fixture therefore checks all three: that sigma >= 0, that the internal energy of a closed system is conserved, and that the total entropy actually rises. Sample states avoid thermal equilibrium, where sigma = 0 identically and the check would be vacuous.

parameters._note: x = [S1, S2] are entropies; U = C1 exp(S1/C1) + C2 exp(S2/C2); T_i = exp(S_i/C_i)

checks.closed_form: sigma = lambda (T1-T2)^2/(T1 T2) >= 0 for all reachable x
dU/dt = T1 dS1/dt + T2 dS2/dt = -Q + Q = 0. A closed two-body system exchanges energy internally and loses none. A model that puts the heat flow in R fails here, which is exactly the intended trap.
S1 + S2 must rise: entropy is created, not merely moved. A model that conserves entropy passes a sigma >= 0 check and fails this one.
